Pakistan vs Bangladesh for Clothing Manufacturing: Which Should Your Brand Choose in 2026?

✎ FABRIOZA Team 📅 July 26, 2026 🔄 Updated: July 26, 2026 ☕ 9 min read
Home › Blog › Pakistan vs Bangladesh
TL;DR: Bangladesh is the volume champion — unbeatable per-unit prices on basic knits and woven bottoms, but typical MOQs of 1,000–3,000 pieces per style. Pakistan wins for small and mid-size brands: MOQs from 20–50 pieces, stronger sportswear/streetwear specialization, and comparable quality at slightly higher per-unit cost. New brands ordering under 1,000 pieces per design are usually better served in Pakistan.

Bangladesh and Pakistan are two of the world's largest apparel exporters, and brands comparing them usually discover the choice is not about which country is "better" — it is about which country matches your order size and product type. This guide compares both honestly, including where Bangladesh clearly beats Pakistan.

Where Bangladesh Wins

If you are ordering 5,000+ pieces of a basic garment — five-pocket denim, plain tees, uniform polos — Bangladesh's giant vertically-integrated factories will usually beat any Pakistani quote by 5–15%%. The country built its industry around exactly this: massive, efficient runs of standardized garments for global retailers. Its duty-free EU access under Everything But Arms has also made it the default for European volume buyers.

Where Pakistan Wins

Pakistan's industry — especially the Sialkot cluster — grew up on sports goods and performance apparel, which demands short runs, frequent design changes and heavy decoration (sublimation, embroidery, appliqué). That heritage means:

  • MOQs a startup can actually order: 50 pieces per style is normal here; a 20-piece trial order is possible. In Bangladesh most factories will not open a line below 1,000 pieces.
  • Sportswear specialization: sublimated soccer kits, basketball uniforms, gym wear and compression fabrics are a core competency, not a side business.
  • Faster small-order lead times: 2–4 weeks versus booking a production slot months out.
  • Cotton at the source: Pakistan grows its own cotton and mills its own fleece and jersey, keeping heavyweight hoodie and tee fabric costs competitive.

Quality and Compliance

Both countries produce export-grade garments and both have factories you should avoid. The differentiator is the individual factory's certifications and QC process, not the flag. Wherever you source, insist on ISO 9001 (quality management), a social audit (amfori BSCI or SMETA), pre-production samples, and in-line + final inspection with photos. That checklist protects you in Dhaka and Sialkot equally.

The Decision Rule

Order volume decides it: under ~1,000 pieces per style, Pakistan; over ~5,000 pieces of basics, Bangladesh; in between, get quotes from both and compare landed cost — not just FOB price. For sportswear and heavily decorated garments, Pakistan at any volume. See how Pakistan stacks up against the other giant in our Pakistan vs China comparison.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Bangladesh cheaper than Pakistan for clothing manufacturing?

On large-volume basics (1,000+ pieces of tees, polos, denim), yes - Bangladesh is usually 5-15% cheaper per unit. On small orders Bangladesh factories either decline or quote surcharges, so Pakistan's 50-piece MOQs make it cheaper in practice for startups.

Which country is better for sportswear and team uniforms?

Pakistan, decisively. The Sialkot cluster is the world's sports-goods manufacturing hub, with deep sublimation, embroidery and performance-fabric capability. Bangladesh's industry is built around volume basics, not decorated sportswear.

What is the minimum order quantity in Bangladesh vs Pakistan?

Typical Bangladesh factories require 1,000-3,000 pieces per style. In Pakistan, 50-300 pieces is common - FABRIOZA's standard MOQ is 50 pieces with a 20-piece trial order option.

Are lead times faster in Pakistan or Bangladesh?

For small orders, Pakistan: 2-4 weeks from approved sample is typical. Bangladesh factories run booked production slots, so 60-120 days is common regardless of order size.

Do Pakistan and Bangladesh have duty-free access to Europe?

As of 2026 both enjoy preferential EU access - Pakistan under GSP+ and Bangladesh under Everything But Arms (with LDC graduation approaching). Rates change, so verify current tariff status for your import country before costing.
